::: {.notes}
Multi-photon imaging is technique we can use to learn about what is going on in the brain, and making sense of this data requires goog analysis tools.

In a typical analysis pipeline, we would typically have these kind of steps in this sequence.

## We are pushing the limits of imaging neural activity with light

<iframe src="https://elifesciences.org/articles/107540/figures#video1" width="100%" height="500" style="border: 0;" allowfullscreen></iframe>

Analysis tools need to be chosen appropriately.

::: {.notes}
* deeper in the brain: three-photon imaging (Cloves + Margrie 2025)
* higher frequency: 
  * voltage imaging
  * various GECI indicators 
* more of the brain: meso-scale imaging
* in a more naturalistic setting: freely moving
* larger volumes: light bead microscopy
* for longer: multiday recordings
* more control: optical stimulation
:::

## To deal with this complexity, we need to coordinate analysis software at a community level

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
![Suite2p logo](img/suite2p_logo.png)
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
![CaImAn logo](img/caiman_logo.png)
:::
::::

Current open-source tools are hard to compare, combine and adapt for more complex data.

::: {.notes}
So there are some widely adopted open-source tools in the functional imaging space. The mostly widely used, as far as I can tell, are Suite2p and CaImAn. Caim have slighly different strengths, but are defacto used interchangeably by researchers. They are great tools, and there are many others. What also happens is that labs make their own pipelines.

All of this has some problems. The tools are not interoperable with each other: if you use the registration algorithm from one, you are locked-into the segmentation step of the same tool. Work is duplicated, and the support for these tools could be better.

So to adapt to our changing needs, we need to improve on this. Areas that could do with improvement are flexibility, guidance, performance, transparency, collaboration. And we can't do this alone, we need feedbac. So we see this more as a social problem rather than a technical problem.

As NIU we have a successful track record of building software for research at a community level.
:::

## PhotonMosaic: functional imaging analysis software at a community level

![headshots of the developer team](img/developer_team.png)

## Photon-mosaic: Vision

* simplicity
* flexibility
* performance
* quality control

## Simplicity

```python
imaging = read_scan_image_imaging(file_path=file_path)

motion = compute_motion(imaging=imaging, method="suite2p")
registered_imaging = register_motion(imaging=imaging, motion=motion)

segmented_rois = run_segmentation(
    registered_imaging,
    method="suite2p",
    algorithm="cellpose",
)

roi_analyzer = create_roi_analyzer(cell_rois, registered_imaging)
roi_analyzer.compute("neuropil")
roi_analyzer.compute("fluorescence", use_neuropil=True)
df_over_f = roi_analyzer.compute("df_over_f").get_data(outputs="recording")
```

## Flexibility

```python
imaging = read_scan_image_imaging(file_path=file_path)

motion = compute_motion(imaging=imaging, method="normcorre")
registered_imaging = register_motion(imaging=imaging, motion=motion)

segmented_rois = run_segmentation(
    registered_imaging,
    method="suite2p",
    algorithm="cellpose",
)

roi_analyzer = create_roi_analyzer(cell_rois, registered_imaging)
roi_analyzer.compute("neuropil")
roi_analyzer.compute("fluorescence", use_neuropil=True)
df_over_f = roi_analyzer.compute("df_over_f").get_data(outputs="recording")
```

::: {.notes}
* Python API wrapping / re-implementing CaImAn + Suite2p
* `spikeinterface`-like design
:::
